name: ratified decisions (ADR index)
description: apps/web is a thin Next.js App Router shell — web-only, logic stays extraction-ready in packages; RSC + Server Actions, TanStack Query where interactive (ADR-0002, ADR-0008).

name: onboarding-wiring
description: apps/web wires Creator Onboarding as a thin shell: browser Better Auth client (magicLink+emailOTP) for the cookie sign-in flow; useChat(DefaultChatTransport) maps UIMessage<->InterviewMessage via prepareSendMessagesRequest so the interview route Zod-validates one shape; profile-gen runs via runAgentStructured with a RESONANCE_FAKES-only injected canned tool-calling model (ai/test), dynamically imported to stay out of prod; commit redirects to the returned profileId because getCreatorProfileById is a profile-PK lookup with no by-user query exposed.

name: web-live-by-default-di
description: apps/web is live-by-default (ADR-0018): Server Actions call the live @resonance/ai seam (runAgentStructured with no injected model -> resolveModel; commit ctx passes resolveEmbedder()). No RESONANCE_FAKES runtime branch and no dynamic import of ai/test in shipped code. Tests inject fakes ONLY via DI: actions.test.ts mocks the @resonance/ai public entrypoint (getSession/runAgentStructured/commitCreatorProfile/resolveEmbedder), so unit tests stay green with zero credentials without ever hitting a live path or the removed env flag. The runner's RunInput.model DI seam stays open but is taken by tests only. The E2E OTP harness (app/api/test/last-otp + e2e/*) is a SEPARATE human-gated seed (resonance-a4a4) and still uses RESONANCE_FAKES on purpose.

name: usechat-onerror-surface
description: Surface live streaming failures in the interview UI (AI SDK v6 / @ai-sdk/react). useChat's onError callback sets a streamError state; the client renders an inline, token-only error card (border-danger + text-danger on bg-surface, role=alert) with a 'Try again' Button (variant=outline size=sm) that calls useChat's regenerate() to re-run the last turn and clears the error. A fresh user turn also clears streamError before the new stream starts. Without this, a resolveModel throw or Gateway failure vanishes and reads as a silent no-response. RTL test pattern: since useChat is mocked, capture the options via vi.mocked(useChat).mock.calls.at(-1)?.[0], narrow-cast to read onError (it lives on the ChatInit arm of the UseChatOptions union, so direct property access fails typecheck), fire it inside act(), then assert the alert renders and retry calls regenerate + clears the surface.

name: e2e-harness-dynamic-import
description: E2E harness must DYNAMIC-import fakes (not static) so they stay out of the prod bundle; centralize the E2E_HARNESS selection in intent-named accessors.

name: session-optional Server Action: viewer resolved server-side, never a query field
description: apps/web/app/(app)/discover/actions.ts. A Server Action that acts on behalf of a user takes TWO things that must not be merged: the Zod-parsed client payload, and the viewer resolved from getWebSession. `searchCreators(input)` parses `input` with CreatorDiscoveryQuerySchema and separately derives `viewer`, then calls `port.searchCreators(query, viewer)` — the DiscoveryPort signature keeps them apart deliberately, so there is NO identity field on the query for a caller to spoof through the search box. Zod's strip-unknown-keys behaviour does the rest: a payload carrying `userId`/`viewer` loses it at the parse line (asserted by a test). Session-optional means viewer===null is a first-class case (every row's followState becomes 'unknown', DiscoveryPort invariant 5), not an auth failure — the route does not redirect. Contrast the follow mutations in the same file, where auth IS required: they return a discriminated { ok:false, reason:'unauthenticated'|'follow_self' } instead of throwing, because the caller is a button inside a results list and a redirect would cost the page of results; follow_self is translated from @resonance/db's typed ResonanceError, and every other error propagates untouched.

A controlled input seeded from a prop with React.useState(prop) goes STALE under a Next.js App Router soft navigation. /discover keeps search + tab state in the URL, and the search field was initialised as useState(query). On a searchParams-only navigation — browser back/forward, or opening a shared /discover?q=... link while already mounted — the App Router re-renders the client component WITHOUT remounting it, so the field kept its old value while the URL and the results moved on. Worse than a cosmetic mismatch: the tab handler calls navigate(nextKind, text), so the next tab click navigated to the STALE ?q=. Caught by the no-mistakes review gate, not by any of the 11 existing RTL tests, because every one of them rendered fresh instead of rerendering with changed props.
resolution: Use React's documented 'adjusting state when props change' pattern — hold the last-seen prop in state and reset the draft DURING render when it differs: const [syncedQuery,setSyncedQuery]=useState(query); if (query!==syncedQuery){setSyncedQuery(query);setText(query);}. Do NOT use useEffect (renders one frame of stale text first) and do NOT key/remount the component from the page (that also discards in-flight follow state). The guard matters: it resyncs only when the PROP changes, so a query the member is midway through typing on the same URL survives. Regression test = RTL rerender() with a changed prop asserting both the field value AND that a subsequent tab click navigates with the new query.

content: Shared app chrome belongs to a route GROUP layout, not to a component. apps/web/app/(app)/layout.tsx renders @resonance/ui's 80px AppNav once for /onboarding/creator, /creator/[id] and /discover; before this it was composed inside interview-client.tsx, so /creator/[id] had no rail and every new in-app route would have re-composed it. A (parenthesised) group adds NO URL segment — verify with next build's route table after moving files. The (onboarding) group stays outside it: signup/verify/start are cardless-on-white with no rail. When you move a screen into the group, reproduce its box model exactly (the layout is 'flex h-screen w-full overflow-hidden' + AppNav + 'flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col overflow-hidden', and each route owns its own scrolling) — the interview screens have captured app.png parity artifacts that a nesting change would invalidate.

description: The 'build the singleton if it is absent' idiom is unsafe when construction is async. apps/web/lib/e2e-harness.ts harnessMailOverride() had an await (a dynamic import) between the 'is it built?' guard and the assignment to its globalThis slot, so the two Better Auth calls the signup form fires in parallel (signIn.magicLink + emailOtp.sendVerificationOtp) both passed the guard on a cold dev server and each built a fake mail. One fake won the globalThis slot the auth instance sends through; the other won the process-wide OTP observation slot registerObservedLoginCodes() writes. peekLoginCode() then read an array nothing pushed into, so GET /api/test/last-otp answered {otp:null} forever and onboarding-creator.spec.ts was red on main. It only reproduces on a COLD server — a warm one has the fake already built, which is why a single warm-up request masked it.
resolution: Store the in-flight PROMISE in the globalThis slot, not the resolved value: 'store[KEY] ??= (async () => {...})()' completes before any await, so concurrent callers all await the same construction. Chain a .catch that deletes the slot and rethrows, so a transient cold-server import failure can be retried instead of caching a rejected promise forever. Do NOT assume a sibling '??=' has the same bug — getWebAuth()'s 'store[KEY] ??= createAuth(...)' is already atomic because createAuth is SYNCHRONOUS, so there is no await between its read and write. Check whether construction awaits before changing it.

description: Relaxing a required Zod field to .optional() in @resonance/core silently changes what downstream 'is this parseable?' guards mean. apps/web /discover used CreatorDiscoveryQuerySchema.safeParse({text: q}) FAILING as its no-query signal. I tried to preserve that with a 'q !== undefined' guard plus a comment claiming the page would otherwise issue personalized searches — but the local first() helper coerces absent params with '?? empty string', so q is ALWAYS a string, the guard was unreachable dead code, and the comment was false. The no-mistakes review step caught it.
resolution: Before adding a guard to protect behaviour after a schema relaxation, read what the value can ACTUALLY be at that call site — here the helper's '?? empty string' made the guarded case unreachable. The real protection already existed and was worth stating instead: .optional() permits an ABSENT field, not an empty string, so '?q=' and a bare route still arrive as text:'' and still fail .min(1). Verify the coercion helper rather than reasoning from the declared type alone.

description: Shipped a new route with a visual surface (/interests) whose picker rendered flush TOP-LEFT instead of centred, because page.tsx returned the form bare under the (onboarding) layout while all three sibling screens (signup, verify, start) wrap theirs in the same '<main className="mx-auto flex min-h-screen max-w-3xl flex-col items-center justify-center px-6">'. The page's own docstring already claimed 'centred content', so the code contradicted its documentation. It survived my verification because I drove the FEATURE in a real browser — chips render, selection persists, personalized rows return — and treated that as verified. Behavioural assertions never look at the page, so functional success laundered an unchecked appearance. The no-mistakes test step caught it visually.
resolution: A new ROUTE with a visual surface needs a visual artifact before claiming it works, the same as a component does (ADR-0019: parity is a diff of two images, never a prose claim). Driving behaviour is not a substitute. Cheapest sufficient check when a full manifest capture is not warranted: screenshot the route and compare its layout against the sibling screens in the same route group — and when adding a page to an existing route group, grep the siblings' wrapper first and copy it, because in this repo the (onboarding) group's centring lives in each page's own <main>, not in the group layout.

name: interest-selection-wiring
description: How Slice B interest selection is wired in apps/web, and why. /interests lives in the (onboarding) route group (own full-page chrome, no AppNav rail) and is reached by EVERY newly verified account: roles are additive, so a creator is also a member and gets a personalized /discover from the same selection. AFTER_VERIFY must match in BOTH verify-form and signup-form or which channel a member used (OTP vs magic link) would change where they land. CENTRING comes from each page own main wrapper in this route group, not the group layout, so a new page must copy the siblings wrapper. Submission is the form NATIVE action, which is what the TopicPicker action prop exists for: the checked chips POST themselves so the step works with JS disabled (ADR-0008), and onSubmit only marks it in-flight so a double-click cannot fire two writes. Pressing Continue with NOTHING selected is a valid empty selection: that is how skip works without inventing a control the design does not draw, and the action must NOT early-return on it, or clearing your topics leaves a stale interest vector still ranking /discover. The member comes from the session, never the payload, since MemberInterestsSchema strips unknown keys. On /discover, an empty query plus a signed-in viewer OMITS THE TEXT FIELD so the port ranks on the stored interest embedding (DiscoveryPort invariant 8); signed out it is not asked at all; a BLANK query still fails min(1) and is NOT personalization. discover-client keys its view off ROWS first, because an empty query can now legitimately have results, and keying idle off the query alone silently swallows every personalized row.
